decks.module: Dealer purchases and Title and registration

cards.front: Complete the rule: Within twenty days after a vehicle purchase, the.
cards.back: Within twenty days after a vehicle purchase, the dealer must send the agency the transaction application, properly signed title or origin certificate and separate payments for title and plate fees and sales tax.
cards.memory_hook: Dealer submits documents and separate payments

cards.front: Complete the rule: Sales tax on a dealer vehicle purchase varies.
cards.back: Sales tax on a dealer vehicle purchase varies with the city or county where the purchase occurs.
cards.memory_hook: Purchase location affects sales tax

cards.front: Complete the rule: Within twenty days of acquiring a vehicle from.
cards.back: Within twenty days of acquiring a vehicle from a private owner, the agency must receive the application, seller-signed title, title and plate payments and vehicle-use-tax payment.
cards.memory_hook: Private purchase has twenty day submission

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a private purchase below fifteen thousand dollars.
cards.back: For a private purchase below fifteen thousand dollars, vehicle-use tax depends on model year; at that price or above it depends on the selling price.
cards.memory_hook: Private use tax basis changes at

cards.front: Complete the rule: The private-party tax submission requires form R U.
cards.back: The private-party tax submission requires form R U T fifty and the correct payment to the state revenue department.
cards.memory_hook: Private tax form goes to revenue

cards.front: Complete the rule: An out-of-state purchase needs the transaction application, title.
cards.back: An out-of-state purchase needs the transaction application, title and plate fees, tax payment, a bill of sale and either the dealer-signed origin certificate for a new vehicle or assigned title for a used one.
cards.memory_hook: Out of state purchase needs origin

cards.front: Complete the rule: When transferring plates to an out-of-state.
cards.back: When transferring plates to an out-of-state purchase, include the recent vehicle-registration identification card.
cards.memory_hook: Plate transfer needs recent registration card

cards.front: Complete the rule: Registration creates a state vehicle record and permits.
cards.back: Registration creates a state vehicle record and permits legal use on Illinois roads, while the Illinois title proves ownership.
cards.memory_hook: Registration and title have different purposes

decks.module: Title and registration and License plates

cards.front: Complete the rule: Every vehicle and mobile home needs a.
cards.back: Every vehicle and mobile home needs a title even when it is not registered.
cards.memory_hook: Title obligation does not depend on

cards.front: Complete the rule: Registration fees are annual, and renewal more than.
cards.back: Registration fees are annual, and renewal more than one month after expiry carries a twenty-dollar late charge.
cards.memory_hook: Annual renewal has late fee threshold

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook lists a one-hundred-fifty-one-dollar annual fee for.
cards.back: The handbook lists a one-hundred-fifty-one-dollar annual fee for a passenger vehicle or a qualifying truck weighing no more than eight thousand pounds.
cards.memory_hook: Listed passenger registration fee has truck

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed motorcycle registration fee is forty-one.
cards.back: The listed motorcycle registration fee is forty-one dollars, while an autocycle registration is seventy-one dollars.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle and autocycle fees differ

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed replacement charge is six dollars for.
cards.back: The listed replacement charge is six dollars for one plate or nine dollars for two plates, and a replacement sticker is twenty dollars.
cards.memory_hook: Replacement plates and sticker have separate

cards.front: Complete the rule: Personalized, vanity and some other plate types carry.
cards.back: Personalized, vanity and some other plate types carry additional fees, and legislation can change the published fee schedule.
cards.memory_hook: Plate extras and law changes affect

cards.front: Complete the rule: Carry the vehicle-registration card in the.
cards.back: Carry the vehicle-registration card in the vehicle or on your person whenever driving.
cards.memory_hook: Registration card accompanies driving

cards.front: Complete the rule: Passenger vehicles, trucks and vans must show a.
cards.back: Passenger vehicles, trucks and vans must show a plate at each end, with frames that leave all plate information visible and no plate covers.
cards.memory_hook: Two plates remain fully visible

cards.front: Complete the rule: Motorcycles, mopeds, trailers, semitrailers and apportioned.
cards.back: Motorcycles, mopeds, trailers, semitrailers and apportioned buses use one plate at the rear.
cards.memory_hook: Listed vehicle types use rear plate

cards.front: Complete the rule: Truck tractors and apportioned straight trucks.
cards.back: Truck tractors and apportioned straight trucks display their single plate at the front.
cards.memory_hook: Listed heavy vehicles use front plate

cards.front: Complete the rule: On sale, remove the plates and keep them.
cards.back: On sale, remove the plates and keep them as the seller because Illinois plates stay with their owner rather than the vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Seller retains plates

cards.front: Complete the rule: A temporary registration permit goes in the rear-plate.
cards.back: A temporary registration permit goes in the rear-plate location and lasts ninety days from issuance, with possible reissuance if plates have not arrived by then.
cards.memory_hook: Temporary registration has rear location and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Replace the temporary permit with permanent plates when.
cards.back: Replace the temporary permit with permanent plates when they arrive, then destroy and discard the removed permit.
cards.memory_hook: Permanent plates replace temporary permit

cards.front: Complete the rule: Temporary registration permits are available from licensed.
cards.back: Temporary registration permits are available from licensed dealers, remittance agencies, currency exchanges and agency facilities.
cards.memory_hook: Temporary permits have authorized issuing channels

cards.front: Complete the rule: A courtesy vehicle-renewal reminder may arrive.
cards.back: A courtesy vehicle-renewal reminder may arrive roughly sixty days before registration expires.
cards.memory_hook: Courtesy reminder is approximate

cards.front: Complete the rule: Registration can be renewed online, by mail, at.
cards.back: Registration can be renewed online, by mail, at an agency facility, through the notice’s telephone service or at participating financial or remittance businesses.
cards.memory_hook: Renewal has several authorized channels

cards.front: Complete the rule: Affix the renewal sticker at the upper-right part.
cards.back: Affix the renewal sticker at the upper-right part of the rear plate promptly; failing to display it after the old sticker expires can lead to a stop and ticket.
cards.memory_hook: New sticker belongs at rear plate’s

cards.front: Complete the rule: An agency receipt kept in the vehicle can.
cards.back: An agency receipt kept in the vehicle can temporarily replace an unreceived sticker purchased online before expiry, but only for thirty days after the old registration sticker expires.
cards.memory_hook: Online purchase receipt has limited grace

cards.front: Complete the rule: An active-duty member or reservist proving combat service.
cards.back: An active-duty member or reservist proving combat service may have the standard registration fee waived for the renewal immediately after returning to the United States.
cards.memory_hook: Combat return renewal waiver needs proof

cards.front: Complete the rule: Qualifying Illinois-resident noncombat military personnel, Armed Forces civilian.
cards.back: Qualifying Illinois-resident noncombat military personnel, Armed Forces civilian employees and Defense Department employees serving abroad have forty-five days after return to obtain or renew vehicle registration.
cards.memory_hook: Qualifying overseas service has return registration

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook advises allowing at least forty-five.
cards.back: The handbook advises allowing at least forty-five days after ordering personalized or vanity plates.
cards.memory_hook: Special plate order needs processing time

cards.front: Complete the rule: Eligible seniors and people with disabilities under the.
cards.back: Eligible seniors and people with disabilities under the Benefit Access Program may receive one annual plate-fee discount for qualifying passenger or recreational vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: Benefit Access discount has eligibility and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicles operated in Illinois need liability coverage for.
cards.back: Vehicles operated in Illinois need liability coverage for injury or damage caused to other people or their property.
cards.memory_hook: Liability coverage protects other persons and

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed minimum liability limit for one person’s.
cards.back: The listed minimum liability limit for one person’s injury or death in a crash is twenty-five thousand dollars.
cards.memory_hook: One person injury minimum is twenty

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed liability minimum for injury or death.
cards.back: The listed liability minimum for injury or death of more than one person in a crash is fifty thousand dollars.
cards.memory_hook: Multiple person injury minimum is fifty

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed minimum for damage to.
cards.back: The listed minimum for damage to another person’s property is twenty thousand dollars.
cards.memory_hook: Property damage minimum is twenty thousand

cards.front: Complete the rule: Some vehicle categories need liability.
cards.back: Some vehicle categories need liability limits above the general minimums.
cards.memory_hook: General minimums do not cover every

cards.front: Complete the rule: Carry liability proof with the driver or vehicle.
cards.back: Carry liability proof with the driver or vehicle and show it when police request it; the insurance card may be paper or displayed electronically.
cards.memory_hook: Insurance proof must be available to

cards.front: Complete the rule: While replacing a missing insurance card, carry another.
cards.back: While replacing a missing insurance card, carry another proof such as a binder, current declarations, certificate or latest payment receipt.
cards.memory_hook: Use alternate proof while replacing card

cards.front: Complete the rule: The agency enforces insurance through random computer checks.
cards.back: The agency enforces insurance through random computer checks and traffic citations and requires paper or electronic coverage proof when plates are renewed.
cards.memory_hook: Insurance is checked at renewal and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Lacking required insurance can bring fines, inability to.
cards.back: Lacking required insurance can bring fines, inability to renew registration and suspension of both driving and registration until proof is supplied.
cards.memory_hook: No insurance can stop renewal and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Providing false insurance information to the agency or.
cards.back: Providing false insurance information to the agency or a renewal remitter can lead to criminal charges and a fine.
cards.memory_hook: False renewal insurance information can be

cards.front: Complete the rule: Some vehicles need an environmental-agency emissions test before.
cards.back: Some vehicles need an environmental-agency emissions test before registration renewal, and owners receive notice of the scheduled testing month and year.
cards.memory_hook: Emissions requirement can condition registration renewal

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook lists all of Cook, DuPage and.
cards.back: The handbook lists all of Cook, DuPage and Lake counties and parts of Kane, Kendall, McHenry, Will, Madison, Monroe and St. Clair as emissions-testing areas.
cards.memory_hook: Testing area can cover all or

cards.front: Complete the rule: Notify the licensing agency after.
cards.back: Notify the licensing agency after moving out of an emissions-testing area.
cards.memory_hook: Move outside testing area requires notification

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Illinois resident with a permanent disability may.
cards.back: An Illinois resident with a permanent disability may obtain disability plates for a vehicle titled to that resident.
cards.memory_hook: Disability plates follow qualifying resident and

cards.front: Complete the rule: A household immediate-family member may obtain two disability-plate.
cards.back: A household immediate-family member may obtain two disability-plate sets when the qualifying disabled person owns no vehicle and depends on others for transportation.
cards.memory_hook: Household transportation exception allows two plate

cards.front: Complete the rule: Eligible organizations transporting people with.
cards.back: Eligible organizations transporting people with disabilities may obtain disability plates.
cards.memory_hook: Qualifying transport organizations may receive plates

cards.front: Complete the rule: Disability license plates do not by themselves.
cards.back: Disability license plates do not by themselves waive parking-meter charges or meter time limits.
cards.memory_hook: Disability plates alone do not waive

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Illinois resident with a physician-certified disability may.
cards.back: An Illinois resident with a physician-certified disability may receive a placard, used only when that person is present and entering or leaving the vehicle in the accessible space.
cards.memory_hook: Placard use requires qualifying person’s presence

cards.front: Complete the rule: A meter-exempt permanent placard requires a qualifying permanent.
cards.back: A meter-exempt permanent placard requires a qualifying permanent disability that significantly limits meter access and waives charges and time limits only at meters allowing more than thirty minutes.
cards.memory_hook: Meter exemption requires specific qualifying placard

cards.front: Complete the rule: An ordinary permanent placard allows accessible-space parking but.
cards.back: An ordinary permanent placard allows accessible-space parking but does not waive meter fees or time limits.
cards.memory_hook: Permanent placard is not automatically meter

cards.front: Complete the rule: A temporary disability placard lasts for the physician-certified.
cards.back: A temporary disability placard lasts for the physician-certified period, up to six months if the state issues it or ninety days if a municipality issues it, and does not waive meter rules.
cards.memory_hook: Temporary placard duration depends on issuer

cards.front: Complete the rule: An organization placard supports free disability transportation and.
cards.back: An organization placard supports free disability transportation and accessible-space use while transporting qualifying people, without waiving meter fees or limits.
cards.memory_hook: Organization placard requires qualifying transport
